correctness.rationale: The main inference is false. BMZ Theorem 3.1 is stated for elementary abelian groups, not only cyclic prime-order groups, and does not require the action on the sphere to be free. In its Step (1), ‘fixed-point free’ concerns the whole-group fixed set. Each involution indeed has two cycles, so its fixed sphere is S⁰, but the full V4 fixed space is the diagonal intersected with its orthogonal complement, hence zero. More directly, the Borel sphere bundle over BV4 has mod-2 transgression d₃ of the sphere generator equal to its Euler class xy(x+y), nonzero: the representation is the sum of the three nontrivial real characters. The record's own w₃ falsifies the asserted breakdown. Its restrictions to the order-two subgroups do vanish, and for the rank-two subgroup fixed bundle the proposed e² is zero by dimension, but neither fact obstructs the whole-group step. For the source of a proposed map, 3-acyclicity gives the claimed degree cutoff via the edge map, not membership of x³y³; index functoriality is indeed in the stated direction. Independently of the equivariant argument, the affine target cell as stated follows from simultaneous medians: for unit normal n each block's median projected coordinate mℓ(n) is continuous and odd, so the two differences with block 0 vanish together by Borsuk–Ulam on S². In each ordered seven-point block take the median as a singleton and match the three lower to the three upper points by different colors. Hall holds because a monochromatic subset of color c has at least 3 minus the number of upper points of color c neighbors, at least its size by the class cap, while a multicolor subset sees all upper points. Ties can be ordered arbitrarily. The common median plane meets all singleton and paired convex hulls. Thus the frozen open-cell remark is not correct for the stated affine parameters either.
residual_risks: The census 2304 correctly counts labeled assignments allowing one empty part, not genuine four-nonempty-part partitions; there are 1872 of the latter. The table itself distinguishes the 432 empty-part cases.

The ancillary mod-2 Betti numbers follow from the join formula: Δ4,3 is a connected closed triangulated surface (vertex links are hexagons and each edge has two incident triangles), χ=0 and Betti (1,2,1). The reduced homology polynomial of the join is 3t²(2t+t²)²; simplex freeness in any Δ4,m holds by column uniqueness, not merely by vertex freeness. The source scripts contain a 74 versus 73 empty-face counting typo and a stale contradictory docstring about freeness; neither repairs the headline.
The direct affine argument does not certify a topological transversal extension for arbitrary continuous maps.

The surviving observations are immediate cycle counts, chessboard join arithmetic, and index functoriality without an independent obstacle or needed certificate for this cell; the affine target has a simple common-median proof.
